items.stem: Excel reports a circular reference when you open a workbook. Which built-in tool lists the cells involved?

options.text: Formulas > Formula Auditing > Error Checking > Circular References
options.rationale: Correct: this lists every cell in the circular chain so you can jump to each.
Slicers filter data; they do not find circular references.
That de-duplicates rows; it is unrelated.
Spelling check does not detect formula loops.

items.explanation: Correct: this lists every cell in the circular chain so you can jump to each.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about Trace Precedents and Trace Dependents are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Precedents are the cells a formula reads from
options.rationale: Correct: precedents feed into the selected formula.

options.text: Dependents are the cells that depend on the selected cell
options.rationale: Correct: dependents are formulas that point at the selected cell.

options.text: Tracing follows references across separate workbooks
options.rationale: The trace tools and the related APIs do not cross workbook boundaries.

options.text: Precedents and dependents mean the same thing
options.rationale: They are opposite directions of the dependency chain.

items.explanation: Correct: precedents feed into the selected formula.

items.stem: A reviewer cannot tell which cells in a model are assumptions and which are calculations. What model-standard practice prevents this?

options.text: Separate inputs, workings and outputs and mark inputs with a consistent convention
options.rationale: Correct: a visible inputs/workings/outputs standard makes assumptions traceable.

options.text: Hide all formulas from the reviewer
options.rationale: Hiding logic makes review harder, not easier.
Text storage breaks calculations and does not clarify roles.

options.text: Delete the assumptions once the model is built

items.explanation: Correct: a visible inputs/workings/outputs standard makes assumptions traceable.
